records.reason: Direct OSCE expert-mission legal assessment of 2022 violations; stronger than later commentary and central to the chapter.
Official PACE accountability resolution on the invasion's civilian harm and war-crimes framing; broad institutional synthesis.
Direct late-2022 annexation escalation record from the same institutional family; distinct event from E0002.
Useful but repetitive legal and policy framing after E0002 and E0003; kept only as secondary corroboration.
Contemporaneous OHCHR casualty and strike assessment from the first month of the invasion.
Broader OHCHR late-September synthesis with verified casualties, detentions, and occupation abuses.
Later OHCHR synthesis adds duration and scope, but overlaps heavily with earlier 2022 OHCHR updates.
Incident-rich HRW cluster-munitions report documenting a distinct attack mechanism.
Investigative HRW dossier on filtration and forced transfers, a separate coercion mechanism.
Geospatial assessment of Mariupol destruction; useful direct evidence on siege-scale civilian harm.
Corroborates filtration and deportation abuses, but it repeats E0009's core mechanism.
Clear NGO account of coerced referenda and annexation illegality; complements official and institutional condemnations.
ICRC note on POW access and legal obligations; useful neutral corroboration on detention conditions.
Neutral late-year POW update; helpful for limits and persistence of access issues, not unique blame attribution.
Pre-invasion strategic interpretation useful for intent context, but not direct evidence.
Post-invasion analysis of miscalculation and aims; interpretive support only.
Secondary policy analysis repeating the invasion's false-justification theme; E0025 and E0026 cover this more directly.
Battlefield assessment, not a direct 2B chapter fact pattern; too far from the core conduct issues.
Reuters account preserves Putin's public rationale and the contemporaneous peace-talk context without later hindsight.
Direct report of Putin's partial mobilization decree, a major in-period escalation.
Later retrospective tying 2023 rhetoric back to 2022 war aims; useful context, not primary 2022 evidence.
Specific Bucha incident is illustrative but overlaps with broader civilian-harm evidence already retained.
UN Secretary-General contemporaneous summary of the war, annexation illegality, and civilian toll.
Official UK condemnation preserves a contemporary allied position, but it is policy framing rather than independent fact-finding.
Concise fact-check of Putin's invasion justifications; good synthesis of false pretexts.
Contemporaneous invasion announcement and broad war start record.
Fact-check adds a concise civilian-targeting rebuttal, but the underlying harm is already better established by OHCHR and HRW.
Contemporaneous negotiation reporting adds peace-process context, but overlaps with E0019.
Reuters explainer via another republisher covering the same March peace-talk and rationale package as E0019.
Shows a shift in stated war aims after Kyiv setbacks, useful for interpretation of strategy.
Interpretive mobilization analysis repeating E0020's direct decree record.
AP-reported mobilization update largely duplicates the direct decree already captured in E0020.
Captures Putin's post-mobilization public framing and escalation rhetoric.
Another Reuters republishment of the mobilization call-up.
A useful limitation on the mobilization decree, showing selective exemptions.
Official Russian self-justification for annexation; repeats state talking points and adds little independent value.
Adds contemporaneous external assessment of Putin's decision environment; interpretive rather than evidentiary.
Contains both the denial and the underlying Bucha allegations; useful as a denial example, not primary proof.
Useful escalation-context example of a Russian dirty-bomb allegation and international rebuttal.
Useful proxy-blame example showing the wider escalation narrative.
Later AP retrospective repeating the same 2023 no-peace-until-goals-met line already captured in E0021.
Early Carnegie strategic reading is helpful for intent context, but it is still analysis.
High-level strategic summary of the invasion's failures; less direct than retained casualty, abuse, and mobilization evidence.
Broad think-tank interpretation of strategic miscalculation, redundant with retained war-aim and escalation records.
Another strategic interpretation of the September escalation; overlaps with E0020 and E0030.

remaining_concerns: Several later analyses and retrospectives overlap the direct 2022 record and were dropped to avoid overweighting commentary.
Official Russian self-justifications are preserved only sparingly as context or contrary material, not as independent evidence.
POW-treatment evidence is strongest on access and abuse patterns; attribution for every detention site remains less granular than the casualty and strike record.
